reviews.title: Co-Star: The Instagram of The Cosmos
reviews.text:
Co–Star feels like the Instagram of the cosmos: polished, provocative, and weirdly committed to making you feel worse about yourself.

Nearly every reading is “trouble in sex and love,” “trouble in relationships,” or another explanation of what you’re doing wrong, avoiding, or failing to become. It doesn’t feel insightful—it feels like fear-mongering dressed up as astrology.

I use several astrology apps, websites, and programs, and none leave me feeling consistently shamed the way Co–Star does. Astrology should provoke reflection and growth. Co–Star mostly provokes anxiety.

At some point, negativity stops being “brutally honest” and just becomes bad guidance.

reviews.title: Used to be amazing
reviews.text: I used to love this app. The horoscopes felt personal, the daily insights were scarily accurate, and it was super fun to use. Now, every horoscope is clearly written with ai, littered with emdashes and adverbs like quietly. It’s disappointing. Part of the allure of CoStar was that it was personal. The first year I started using it, not a single horoscope repeated; now I check the app and I have the same dos and don’ts and day-at-a-glance at least 5 times a month. Either the creators sold the company or they got lazy and started using AI. As a true believer in astrology, I loved the specific advice. Everything feels so vague that I don’t believe what the app says anymore. It’s marketed as “personalized astrology” but both the insights on the app and Co-Stars social media presence feels so inaccurate and impersonal that it makes me angry. I deleted my account because it’s a shame that such a special app was ruined by AI.

reviews.title: The most unfriendly customer service
reviews.text: I was trying to subscribe a month of the premium to see if I liked it and somehow ordered a year. I’m sure it was an oversight on my part, but there’s a huge difference between the cost. I immediately cancelled the subscription and sent them an email requesting to immediately cancel the year and refund my money bc I wasn’t planning on spending the $50 on some horoscope app. Well it has taken them over a week to initially respond and they obviously didn’t look into my request because I got a generic answer telling me to do what I’d already done and I was requesting for a refund. Apple told me they need to process the cancellation of my subscription before I can get my money back and this girl, days later, tells me the same thing she said in her last email which was useless. They don’t even read your emails. Total trash company. I can get my horoscope out of the newspaper from now on.

reviews.title: Co-Star Ruins Your Day — Always, Everyday
reviews.text:
I believe in horoscopes and finding an understanding of yourself in a power that is bigger than you.

Including  “real talk” horoscope readings that offer constructive criticism keeps a source credible and encourages productive growth. 

Making everyone feel like they were born in an especially unfortunate astrological time/planetary position/month/year and that they are cosmically doomed is not ok. 

This app is run by people who will exclusively give you the worst case scenario so you pay for good news. And unfortunately, I did the premiums because my friends were - and I’ve since corroborated the consistent negativity and gotten people off of it. 

If you want to grow as a person, this is not the app to help you. Do not waste your money or time even considering this mean babble as important.

There is no longer any point to this app unless you want a daily sentence that barely makes sense at all as a written sentence, let alone something that is supposed to apply to you. reviews.text:
Initially it was great! I used it for years… even had paid for a profile to put my partners details into it to use as a tool to help navigate our relationship…

However after a couple of years later when I realized I had entered the wrong year into my partner’s information (that I could not edit, I could only delete and purchase a new one). 
It feels like the app had assumed I went through a break up (or still going through one, which is weird coz I am still happily married). 
Anyways since this happened the daily information it gives me is all around relationships and trusting again! I have not related to this app since and  i would delete if I hadn’t already invested a decent amount of $$$ around its other features it offers…. It feels broken all because I could not edit a date I had purchased years ago.

Bottom line, when you’re happily married for over a decade and your astrology app is telling you “you’ll find love again” is not insightful it’s just annoying!
